finding.claim: DELETE /projects/:id deletes any project without an ownership or admin check because the result of authorized() is discarded.
finding.source: api.js:16 DELETE /projects/:id, with :id from req.params.id (api.js:17), by any authenticated user

trace.note: Project loaded by attacker-supplied id, no ownership scoping in query
authorized(req.user, project) called; boolean return value discarded

finding.guards_checked: authorized() at api.js:12-14 is a correct predicate (ownerId === user.id or isAdmin === true) but its return value is unused at api.js:18. authorize() at api.js:4-10 would throw correctly and is used by the sibling PUT handler at api.js:25, so the DELETE handler is the one missing the check. No other middleware is visible in the repo.

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 is called at api.js:18 but its boolean return is discarded, so it never blocks anything. authorize() (api.js:4-10, throws on failure) is not called on the DELETE path; it is only used by the PUT handler at api.js:25. No other middleware is in the repo (Glob shows only api.js).
verdict.reason: The DELETE handler at api.js:18 calls authorized(req.user, project) as a bare statement, discarding its boolean result, so api.js:19 deletes the project for any caller that reaches the route. The attacker only needs to be an authenticated low-privilege user, since an anonymous request would throw at api.js:13 when req.user is undefined.
